question: Under Idaho's CDL program, which vehicles fall into Class A?
choice_a: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_b: Any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is in excess of 10,000 pounds
choice_c: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,000 pounds or less that hauls placarded hazardous materials
choice_d: Any vehicle designed to transport fewer than 16 passengers
explanation: The Idaho CDL Classes table defines Class A as any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed exceeds 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classes Table, Class A

question: How does the Idaho CDL manual define a Class B vehicle?
choice_a: Any combination vehicle with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_b: Any vehicle used exclusively to haul hazardous materials
choice_c: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more; these vehicles can tow a vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR
choice_d: Any vehicle designed to carry 16 or more passengers only
explanation: Class B is any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, and such vehicles may tow a vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classes Table, Class B

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,000 pounds or less is included in Idaho's Class C only if it meets which condition?
choice_a: It is owned by a government agency
choice_b: It is hauling placarded hazardous materials or is designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver
choice_d: It is registered for interstate commerce
explanation: Class C covers a single vehicle of 26,000 pounds GVWR or less that is hauling placarded hazardous materials or designed to transport 16 or more passengers including the driver; these vehicles can tow a vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL Classes Table, Class C

question: According to Figure 1.1 (Determining Class of CDL Required), if the GCWR is 26,001 pounds or more AND the GVWR of the trailer/towed unit is 10,001 pounds or more, which class of CDL is required?
choice_a: Class C
choice_b: Class B
choice_d: No CDL is required in this scenario
explanation: Figure 1.1 walks through the decision logic: if the GCWR is 26,001 pounds or more and the GVWR of the towed unit exceeds 10,000 pounds, a Class A CDL is required.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Figure 1.1 Determining Class of CDL Required

question: According to the manual, which of the following requires you to have a CDL?
choice_a: A single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_b: A personal pickup truck used only for commuting
choice_c: Any vehicle registered to a business
choice_d: A trailer weighing less than 5,000 pounds towed by a personal car
explanation: The manual lists a single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more as one of the categories requiring a CDL, along with certain combination vehicles, passenger-carrying vehicles, and hazmat-placarded vehicles.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, You Must Have a CDL to Operate

question: Besides the weight-based thresholds, what other condition requires a CDL regardless of the vehicle's size?
choice_a: The vehicle is more than five years old
choice_b: Any size vehicle which requires hazardous material placards or is carrying material listed as a select agent or toxin under 42 CFR part 73
choice_c: The vehicle is leased rather than owned
choice_d: The vehicle is driven more than 100 miles per day
explanation: The manual states you must have a CDL to operate any size vehicle which requires hazardous material placards, or is carrying material listed as a select agent or toxin in 42 CFR part 73, regardless of the vehicle's weight.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, You Must Have a CDL to Operate

question: Which endorsement is required for combination vehicles pulling double or triple trailers?
choice_a: The N endorsement
choice_b: The X endorsement
explanation: The Idaho endorsements table lists T as the endorsement for combination vehicles with double or triple trailers, requiring the Doubles/Triple Trailers knowledge test.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements Table, T

question: The Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement is required if you want to haul liquid or gaseous materials in a tank meeting what capacity thresholds?
choice_a: An individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_b: Any tank at all, regardless of size
choice_c: An individual rated capacity of exactly 500 gallons
choice_d: An aggregate rated capacity of 119 gallons only
explanation: The manual states the Tank Vehicle Test is required if you want to haul liquid or gaseous materials in a tank or tanks having an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more, whether permanently or temporarily attached to the vehicle or chassis.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests, Tank Vehicle Test

question: What must a driver do in addition to passing a written exam to obtain the H (hazardous materials) endorsement?
choice_a: Nothing further is required
choice_b: Pass a Transportation Security Administration (TSA) background check
choice_c: Complete a separate road test only
explanation: The manual states that to obtain the Hazardous Materials endorsement you are also required to pass a TSA background check, in addition to passing the Hazardous Materials Test.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests, Hazardous Materials Test

question: Which endorsement is required for any vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver?
choice_a: The S endorsement
choice_b: The N endorsement
explanation: The Idaho endorsements table lists P as required for any vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver, and requires the Passenger Vehicles knowledge test.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements Table, P

question: The S (school bus) endorsement applies to a vehicle used to transport students in which circumstances?
choice_a: Only when transporting students on interstate field trips
choice_b: Transporting preprimary, primary, or secondary school students from home to school, school to home, or to and from school-sponsored events
choice_d: Only when the driver is a certified teacher
explanation: The endorsements table describes the S endorsement as applying to any vehicle used to transport preprimary, primary, or secondary school students from home to school, school to home, or to and from school-sponsored events.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements Table, S

question: What does the X endorsement represent on an Idaho CDL?
choice_a: A restriction that prevents the driver from carrying any passengers
choice_b: An endorsement solely for double and triple trailers
choice_c: A combination endorsement representing the hazardous materials and tank vehicles endorsements together
explanation: The manual describes the X endorsement as a combination endorsement representing both the hazardous materials and tank vehicles endorsements, requiring the Tank Vehicles and Hazardous Materials knowledge tests.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Endorsements Table, X

question: What is the fee for a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) in Idaho, according to the CDL license fee schedule?
explanation: The CDL License Fees schedule lists the Commercial Learner's Permit fee as $29.00.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL License Fees

question: Where can an Idaho CDL applicant complete the medical self-certification required under the medical documentation requirements?
choice_a: Only by mail to the FMCSA
choice_b: At a county driver's license office, or online at the ITD self-certification website
choice_c: Only at a private medical examiner's office
choice_d: Self-certification is not required in Idaho
explanation: The manual states self-certification can be accomplished at your county driver's license office, or you can complete your own self-certification on the ITD website at http://dmvapps.itd.idaho.gov/cdlselfcertification.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.2 Medical Documentation Requirements

question: What happens if a driver who is required to have a 'certified' medical status fails to provide and keep up-to-date their medical examiner's certificate?
choice_a: Nothing, as long as they verbally confirm their status
choice_b: They become 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL
explanation: The manual warns that if a driver required to have a certified medical status fails to provide and keep up-to-date their medical examiner's certificate, they become 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.2 Medical Documentation Requirements

question: A driver who operates in Non-Excepted Interstate Commerce is required to provide which document to the State Driver Licensing Agency?
choice_a: A current medical examiner's certificate (DOT card) under 49 CFR 391.45
choice_b: A copy of their vehicle registration only
choice_d: Nothing; Non-Excepted drivers are exempt from medical requirements
explanation: The manual states that if you operate in Non-Excepted Interstate Commerce, you are required to provide a current medical examiner's certificate under 49 CFR 391.45, commonly referred to as a medical certificate or DOT card, to your SDLA.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.2.2 Inter/Intrastate Commerce: Status Non-excepted or Excepted

question: Which knowledge test must be taken by every CDL applicant, regardless of vehicle class or endorsement?
choice_a: The Air Brakes Test
choice_b: The Combination Vehicles Test
explanation: The manual states the General Knowledge Test is taken by all applicants, while the other tests (Passenger, Air Brakes, Combination Vehicles, Hazmat, Tank Vehicle, Doubles/Triples, School Bus) apply only to specific vehicle types or endorsements.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests

question: Which knowledge test must be taken by all bus driver applicants?
choice_a: The Doubles/Triples Test
choice_b: The Passenger Test
explanation: The manual lists the Passenger Test as being taken by all bus driver applicants, in addition to the General Knowledge Test that all applicants must take.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests

question: How long do CDL knowledge test results remain valid in Idaho?
choice_a: 30 days from the date passed
choice_b: Six months from the date passed
choice_c: One year from the date passed
explanation: The manual notes: 'All test results will remain valid for one year from the date they were passed.'
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests

question: How many questions are on Idaho's CDL General Knowledge test, and how many must you answer correctly to pass?
choice_a: 30 questions, 24 correct
choice_b: 50 questions, 40 correct
explanation: The Knowledge Test Information table lists the General Knowledge test as having 50 questions, with a minimum of 40 correct answers required to pass.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Knowledge Test Information Table

question: According to the Knowledge Test Information table, how many questions are on the Hazmat knowledge test, and how many must be answered correctly to pass?
choice_a: 50 questions, 40 correct
choice_b: 25 questions, 20 correct
explanation: The table lists the Hazmat test as having 30 questions, with a minimum of 24 correct answers required to pass.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Knowledge Test Information Table

question: According to the Knowledge Test Information table, how many questions are on the Air Brake knowledge test, and how many must be answered correctly to pass?
choice_a: 25 questions, 20 correct
choice_b: 20 questions, 16 correct
explanation: The table lists the Air Brake test as having 25 questions, with a minimum of 20 correct answers required to pass.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Knowledge Test Information Table

question: According to the Knowledge Test Information table, the Combination Vehicles, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples, Passenger Vehicles, and School Busses knowledge tests all share what question count and passing score?
choice_a: 25 questions, 20 correct to pass
choice_b: 50 questions, 40 correct to pass
explanation: The Knowledge Test Information table lists 20 questions with a minimum of 16 correct answers to pass for each of the Combination Vehicles, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples, Passenger Vehicles, and School Busses tests.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Knowledge Test Information Table

question: Comparing the numbers in Idaho's Knowledge Test Information table (for example, 40 of 50 on General Knowledge, 24 of 30 on Hazmat, 20 of 25 on Air Brake, and 16 of 20 on the remaining tests), what minimum passing percentage do all of Idaho's CDL knowledge tests share?
choice_a: 70 percent
choice_b: 75 percent
explanation: Every test in the Knowledge Test Information table works out to an 80% minimum passing score (e.g., 40/50, 24/30, 20/25, 16/20), matching the federally standardized passing threshold in 49 CFR 383.135(a).
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Knowledge Test Information Table

question: What are the three general types of skills that are tested on the Idaho CDL practical (skills) test?
choice_a: Parallel parking, highway merging, and backing
choice_b: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving
choice_c: Written essay, vision test, and reaction time
explanation: The manual states there are three types of general skills that will be tested: vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving, and you must take these tests in the type of vehicle for which you wish to be licensed.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.1.2 Skills Tests

question: How far in advance are examiners required to notify ITD of a scheduled skills test?
choice_a: At least 24 hours prior
choice_b: At least 7 days prior
explanation: The manual notes that examiners are required to notify ITD of your skills test a minimum of 48 hours prior to the test taking place.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.1.2 Skills Tests

question: According to the CDL License Fees schedule, how much does a four-year CDL cost for an applicant age 21 or over?
explanation: The CDL License Fees schedule lists a four-year CDL for applicants age 21 and over at $40.00 (compared to $15.00 for a one-year CDL at age 20, $30.00 for a three-year CDL age 18 to 21, and $60.00 for an eight-year CDL age 21 and over).
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL License Fees

question: How much does Idaho charge for each written (knowledge) test taken as part of the CDL process?
explanation: The CDL License Fees schedule lists written tests at $5.00 each.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL License Fees

question: What does the CDL License Fees schedule list as the fee to add an endorsement after a CDL has already been issued?
choice_a: $20.00, which does not include the written test fee
choice_b: $5.00, which includes the written test fee
choice_c: $30.00, which includes the written test fee
choice_d: No fee is charged to add an endorsement
explanation: The fee schedule lists 'Add Endorsement (after issuance of a CDL, does not include written test fee)' at $20.00; the written test fee of $5.00 per test is charged separately.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, CDL License Fees

question: How much prior licensed driving experience must you have in order to obtain an Idaho CDL, per Idaho Code 49-303(4)?
choice_a: No prior experience is required
choice_b: At least six months
explanation: The manual states you must have at least one year of licensed driving experience in order to obtain a CDL, per Idaho Code 49-303(4).
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, Age/Experience Requirement

question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes it illegal to operate a CMV in Idaho, and what is the minimum disqualification for a first offense?
choice_a: 0.08% or more; disqualification for at least 90 days
choice_b: 0.04% or more; disqualification for at least one year
choice_d: Any detectable amount; disqualification for life
explanation: The manual states it is illegal to operate a CMV if your BAC is .04% or more, and you will lose your CDL for at least one year for a first offense involving BAC of .04% or higher.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: How long will you lose your CDL if a disqualifying alcohol or drug offense occurs while you are operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials?
choice_a: At least 90 days
choice_b: At least one year
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least three years if the disqualifying offense occurs while you are operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: What is the disqualification for a second alcohol-related major offense, or for using a CMV to commit a felony involving controlled substances?
choice_a: An additional 90 days
choice_b: Three years
choice_d: A $5,000 fine only, with no license impact
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for life for a second offense, and you will also lose your CDL for life if you use a CMV to commit a felony involving controlled substances.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: What happens if you are found to have any detectable amount of alcohol under .04% while operating a CMV?
choice_a: You are put out-of-service for 24 hours
choice_b: You automatically lose your CDL for one year
choice_c: Nothing, since it is below the legal threshold
explanation: The manual states you will be put out-of-service for 24 hours if you have any detectable amount of alcohol under .04%.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: What speed threshold qualifies as 'excessive speeding,' a serious traffic violation, under Idaho's CDL disqualification rules?
choice_a: Any speed 5 mph or more above the posted limit
choice_b: Any speed 15 mph or more above the posted speed limit
choice_c: Any speed over 65 mph regardless of the posted limit
choice_d: Any speed 25 mph or more above the posted limit
explanation: The manual defines excessive speeding, one of the enumerated serious traffic violations, as any speed 15 mph or more above the posted limit.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.3 Serious Traffic Violations

question: How long will you lose your CDL if you commit two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV, versus three or more?
choice_a: 30 days for two; 60 days for three or more
choice_b: At least 60 days for two; at least 120 days for three or more
choice_c: At least 90 days for two; one year for three or more
choice_d: There is no penalty until a fourth violation
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least 60 days if you have committed two serious traffic violations within a three-year period, and for at least 120 days for three or more serious traffic violations within a three-year period.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.3 Serious Traffic Violations

question: What is the CDL disqualification period for a first violation of an out-of-service order, compared to a second violation within a ten-year period?
choice_a: At least 30 days for the first; 90 days for the second
choice_b: At least 90 days for the first; at least one year for the second within a ten-year period
choice_c: At least 60 days for the first; three years for the second
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least 90 days for your first violation of an out-of-service order, and for at least one year if you have committed two violations of an out-of-service order in a ten-year period (at least three years for three or more).
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.4 Violation of Out-of-Service Orders

question: Which of the following will cause you to be denied, or to lose, your hazardous materials endorsement, according to the manual?
choice_a: Being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
choice_b: Having a valid passport
choice_c: Not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States, or being wanted or under indictment for certain felonies
choice_d: Having more than one year of driving experience
explanation: The manual lists several disqualifiers for the hazmat endorsement background check, including not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States, renouncing U.S. citizenship, and being wanted or under indictment for certain felonies.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.6 Hazardous Materials Endorsement Background Check and Disqualifications

question: If you hold a hazardous materials endorsement and are convicted of a disqualifying crime, how quickly must you notify and surrender your hazmat endorsement to the state that issued your CDL?
choice_a: Within 24 hours
choice_b: Within 30 days
explanation: The manual states that if you have a hazardous materials endorsement you must notify and surrender your hazardous materials endorsement to the state that issued your CDL within 24 hours of any conviction or indictment for a disqualifying crime listed in 49 CFR 1572.103, or if adjudicated a mental defective or committed to a mental institution, or if you renounce your U.S. citizenship.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.4 Other CDL Rules

question: What is the CDL disqualification for a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation, compared to a second violation within a three-year period?
choice_a: At least 60 days for the first; at least 120 days for the second within a three-year period
choice_b: At least 30 days for the first; 60 days for the second
choice_c: At least 90 days for the first; one year for the second
choice_d: There is no disqualification for a first violation
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least 60 days for your first railroad-highway grade crossing violation, for at least 120 days for your second violation within a three-year period, and for at least one year for your third violation within a three-year period.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.3.5 Railroad-highway Grade Crossing Violations

question: What happens if a CDL holder breaks the rule against holding more than one license?
choice_a: Nothing, as long as the licenses are from different states
choice_b: A court may fine the driver up to $5,000 or put them in jail, keep the home state license, and return any others
choice_c: The driver simply pays a $20 duplicate fee
choice_d: The driver's medical certificate is automatically revoked
explanation: The manual states you cannot have more than one license; if you break this rule, a court may fine you up to $5,000 or put you in jail, and keep your home state license while returning any others.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.4 Other CDL Rules

question: What is a CDL holder prohibited from doing regarding mobile telephones while driving, per the manual?
choice_a: Nothing; mobile phone use is unrestricted for CDL holders
choice_b: Holding a mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication, dialing by pressing more than a single button, or sending or reading text messages
choice_d: Using a phone is allowed as long as the vehicle is stopped at a light
explanation: The manual states you are not allowed to hold a mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication or dial a mobile telephone by pressing more than a single button when driving, and you are not allowed to send or read text messages while driving.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.4 Other CDL Rules

question: Why must a CDL holder be properly restrained by a safety belt at all times while operating a CMV, according to the manual?
choice_a: Because it is only a suggestion, not a rule
choice_b: Because it is required only for drivers under age 25
choice_c: Because unbelted drivers are four times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle, and the belt helps the driver control the vehicle during a crash
explanation: The manual explains that the safety belt holds the driver securely behind the wheel during a crash, helping the driver control the vehicle and reducing the chance of serious injury or death; if you do not wear a safety belt, you are four times more likely to be fatally injured if you are thrown from the vehicle.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, 1.4 Other CDL Rules
